title: Nerve taps, paddling rolls and who originated them
summary: Green explains single and double taps, calls nerve tap religious, and credits Billy Adams, Groundhog, Billy Yates and Baby Lawrence with the paddling roll.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, it's because if you separate the nerve tap and put it on two feet instead of one, which is single and double, see, you make two beats with any foot, that was considered tap dancing, you see. So the nerve -- the separation, the difference between the two is that one -- the nerve tap is actually like standing on one foot and shaking one foot, you know, and like trembling, you see? It's very religious, you see, because it was a form of happy -- what they call happy, happy. I don't intend to be -- no disrespects, I'll say, but in churches, sometimes.
This seemed to me to be a heavy mix. I notice cramp rolls and sort of like a paddling roll, a mixture of lots of things that you have to be technically superb to do.

Yes. Well, the paddling and roll always be a superb tap dance, because right now it's supposed to be the juvenile of tap dancing, it's the newest work of tap dancing, you see. If At the Hoofer's Club, it was still in being, this would be considered a degree from the Hoofer's Club fraternity, for making a good picture. (recording interruption)

I just said to you, Chuck, that that looked to me like cramps and paddling rolls and things. Was that a little bit before the paddling roll really became the paddling roll and the cramp? So, let me see, now, I would say that Freddie James probably inspired whoever it was, and that would be interesting to know who did, who was the first person who did bring about the paddling roll and the cramp? Because you say that wasn't quite the paddling roll and it wasn't quite a cramp. So it's obviously whoever were the first people to do that, they were inspired by Freddie James. Could you --

Yeah. Well, there were three of them that were inspired by Freddie James, but the original paddling roll came from a tap dancer known as Billy Adams and Ground Hog, see, and then there was Billy Yates and Baby Lawrence.
He was the modernistic debonair, what you would call. I called him the youngest pioneer that came into being of tap dancing, and --

Yes. The late, great Baby Lawrence. I called him Bravery, because he feared no sounds. And he always inspired all the other tap dancers. In fact, he was the cause of a brotherhood of tap dancers which occurred in New York's Jazz Museum here.
